div.head: II Cn 30.3b
div.ab: And gif he þonne fúl weorðe, æt ðam forman cyrre bete ðam teonde twygylde ⁊ þam hlaforde his wer, þe his wites wyrðe sig, ⁊ sette getrywe borgas, þæt he ælces yfeles eft geswice.
⁊ gyf he ðonne ful wurðe, æt ðam forman cyrre bete ðam teonde twygylde ⁊ ðam hlaford his wér, ðe his wites wyrðe sy, ⁊ sette getreowe borgas, þæt he ælces yfeles geswice.
And he þonne ful weorðe, æt þam forman cere bete þam teonde twygylde ⁊ þam hlaforde his wer, þe þæs wyrðe sy, ⁊ sette getrywe borgas, þæt he alces yfeles eft geswyce.
Et si reus fuerit, in prima uice sit calumpniatori duplo reddens et domino suo weram suam, qui ea dignus erit, et ponat credibiles plegios, quod omni malo deinceps abstineat.
Quodsi reus fuerit et in iudicio ceciderit, prima uice ante alia reddat calumniantibus dupliciter sua, et dominis illorum pretium eorum, et postea inueniant fideiussores, quod deinde cessabunt.

Si autem calumpniatus in ipso iudicio deciderit, prima uice emendet calumpniatori duplum et suo domino suam redempcionem, qui forisfactura illius dignus sit, deinde ponat fideiussores, quod deinceps tale facinus cauebit.
⁊ gyf he ðonne ful wurðe, æt ðam forman cyrre bete ðam teonde twygylde ⁊ ðam hlaford his wér ðe his wites wyrðe sy ⁊ sette getreowe borgas, þæt he ælces yfeles geswice.
And gif he þonne ful weorðe, æt ðam forman cyrre bete ðam teonde twygylde and þam hlaforde his wer, þe his wites wyrðe sig, and sette getrywe borgas þæt he ælces yfeles eft geswice.

Und wenn [Verklagt]er nun schuldig befunden wird, büsse er beim ersten Male dem Kläger [den Schaden] doppelt und dem Herrn, [sofern] der (dazu A) berechtigt ist zu dem [durch Verklagten zu verwirkenden] Strafgelde, sein Wergeld und stelle vertrauenswürdige Bürgen [dafür], dass er jeder Missethat fortan sich enthalten werde.

And if [the accused] is then found guilty, let him pay the plaintiff double [the damage] the first time, and the lord — [if] he is entitled (to it, A) to the fine [to be forfeited by the accused] — his wergild, and provide trustworthy sureties [to the effect] that he will refrain from all wrongdoing in future.

And if then he (the accused) is proved guilty, on the first occasion he shall pay double value to the accuser and his wergeld to the lord who is entitled to receive his fine, and he shall appoint trustworthy sureties, that henceforth he will desist from all wrong-doing.

And if he is then convicted, on the first occasion he is to pay two-fold compensation to the accuser and his wergild to the lord who is entitled to his fine, and to appoint trustworthy sureties that he will afterwards cease from all evil-doing.

And then if the accused is proven guilty, the first time he shall pay twice the fine to his accuser and the value of his wergild to his lord, who is entitled to receive his fine, and he shall choose trustworthy sureties to guarantee that he will afterward cease from all wrongdoing.

Cnut erklärt das in seiner Quelle zweideutige Wort ‘Herr’, welches er u. 48, 1 doch selbst anwendet, als ‘Strafgeldempfänger’. Hier ist Inst undeutlicher als u. 30, 6
